dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Is there something I can help you with?

choices.text: Why do you think that Nacker is still alive?

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Considering the interests of the Institute and my personal point of view...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: I do, in fact, hope that both he and that Arkhium Kinetic Core were obliterated in that explosion.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: That would mean that the last traces of Edwin Eastinghouse's influence here would be gone for good.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: But like I said earlier, that explosion was actually a small-scale Arkhium fragment resonance.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Moreover... most of the Arkhium fragments in the explosion radius were ore waste that have been fully depleted of energy.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Logically speaking, even if a large Arkhium chunk had gone out of control, causing the ore waste to resonate, such a violent explosion should not have occurred.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: The only possibility is that someone specially collected Arkhium that has not been depleted from other areas and piled them here.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: They then overloaded that large Arkhium chunk on purpose to create an Arkhium resonance, so as to trigger an explosion to cover up certain traces that would've existed otherwise.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Nacker has always conducted research with Edwin and has a good understanding of the nature of Arkhium. It wouldn't take him much effort to do something like this.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Still, that's just my preliminary conjecture. As for what happens next... we'll need to wait for the research institute to conduct a more detailed investigation.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But why did he steal this core?

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: This Arkhium Kinetic Core is the most cutting-edge technology created by the Fontaine Research Institute to date.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: It wouldn't be a bad idea to sell it or use it in the development of another project, hmph...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: But considering his level of academic expertise... I would rather he sell this Arkhium Kinetic Core for a good price.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Before we discuss this further, I believe Nacker or Ms. Chronie must have mentioned something to you already.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: They must have told you that my research projects and those of Edwin Eastinghouse had some overlap.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: But this is not entirely accurate... In fact, this Arkhium Kinetic Core is the fruit of my joint research with him.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: In theory, if we constantly inject this kinetic core with enough energy, it can easily allow the Experimental Field Generator to run at full power...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: After creating this core, we both realized a problem. We could barely find any way to keep injecting it with enough energy to keep it at maximum power.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Edwin and I tried powering it with a mixture of Pneumousia and Arkhium energy, or by connecting large numbers of Arkhium ores in series to create a super-powered group... but neither worked.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: That was the situation until we found that giant Arkhium... Although it was always in an inert state, Edwin and I were certain that this ore had unprecedented purity.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: We believed that with the right treatment, this ore could definitely output the large amount of energy we needed...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: But then Edwin and I had a disagreement. I offered a up a more conservative proposal, but he wanted... to solve the problem rather more quickly.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: You should know everything else that happened after that.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: He was a genius in the field of scientific research. It's no exaggeration to say that his talent was only second to our first director, Alain Guillotin.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: At the same time, he was an... inhuman monster.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Nothing mattered to him other than his scientific research.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Edwin was willing to do anything or pay any price to advance his research.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: He once told me that research results were the only remuneration he needed. He said:

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: "I don't need any remuneration. To me, research itself is the best reward."

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: However, even though Edwin was a pure researcher, the people under him were all experts... in furthering their own interests, that is.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Some secretly sold research assets, some plagiarized research results, and some used his name to scam others.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: They ruined the Fontaine Research Institute's reputation, little by little.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Like I said before, as long as his research could advance, Edwin wouldn't do anything about this.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: In this way, they used Edwin's name to take all the Institute's resources for themselves.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: The Institute could only continue to conduct detailed reviews on the personnel and funding of Edwin's project team. Mr. Choiseul led many of these review operations personally.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: However, in the mouths of such people, these actions were construed as bureaucratic arrogance and distrust of researchers.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: More and more conflicts took place between us... and no one knew how to resolve them.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: But now... those conflicts no longer exist.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Haha, your question is not a technical one, but rather, an administrative one.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: I think you should ask Mr. Choiseul about this instead.

choices.text: Why do you think Nacker stole the core?

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Do you still remember me flipping through the pictures Ms. Chronie took in the ruins?

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: There's one of Nacker working in front of the suppression device. It's quite blurry... but I'm quite certain that his actions are definitely not part of any operational procedure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That doesn't really mean anything, though. Maybe... maybe a thief came flying across from the nearby mountain and stole the core?

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Heh, that's most definitely impossible. The energy flow of the Arkhium here is the best anti-theft measure there is. No ordinary person can withstand it.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Besides, the timing of the Experimental Field Generator's activation is simply too perfect. It cannot be a mere coincidence...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: I have a preliminary conjecture. Nacker... or should I say, the one who stole the core likely removed the Arkhium Kinetic Core early on, activating the backup energy source.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: However, Pneumousia Cores are relatively inefficient energy sources, and they have to keep up a continuous output of energy to reach the activation threshold of this contraption here.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Hence, this person intentionally activated that large Arkhium chunk, creating a modest, but rather noticeable explosion.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: This way, when the Institute sent someone to investigate, they would be certain to fix the Arkhium Inhibitor first.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: And by the time they realized that they'd have to go to the Experimental Field Generator to retrieve the backup energy supply, the Generator would have already finished charging.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: From a technical perspective, such a modus operandi is highly probable, and those within the Institute capable of doing this would only be Edwin, Mr. Nacker, and myself.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: I doubt Edwin had the opportunity to do anything to that effect... which leaves two remaining suspects. Myself, and Mr. Nacker.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Maybe this was all your doing, then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! You said that Nacker lied, but you've also been lying all along!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe this was all just part of your plan, and you tricked us into escorting you here so you could grab whatever it was you wanted.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Your accusation is not entirely baseless. After this, I will also apply for and submit myself to the Institute's credibility review.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: As far as I'm concerned, though, Mr. Nacker is the one more likely to have committed this act. If this really was his doing, then he should be the one with the most to gain from it.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Even if I am listed alongside him as a suspect... his chances of being convicted are certainly greater than mine.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Bye. I hope you have a good day.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: Ah! If it isn't our Honorary Senior Researcher. Welcome!

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: Can I help you with anything? Or have you come to help me with something instead? Hahaha!

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: Everything is good! It's better than ever! Now that that egomaniac Edwin is gone, the gang of thieves under him no longer exists either.

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: More importantly, the Institute has a chance to be reborn!

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: We can take off the shackles and burdens of the past to focus wholeheartedly on building our foundations once again — that is, to work hard for the well-being of all the people of the Court of Fontaine.

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: I'm currently gathering some people and preparing a Code of Conduct for our organization.

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: It will include principles on the use of funds, research asset management methods... and ethical standards that should be observed in scientific research and work.

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: All research-related behavior at our Institute will have relevant rules and provisions.

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: Ah... What a wonderful future! It's simply the best!

choices.text: Do you and Raimondo run things together?

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: No, to be precise, we deal with affairs related to different areas.

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: Raimondo is responsible for getting scientific work and research back on track, and I'm responsible for everything apart from that.

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: For example, I'm responsible for arranging funds related to manpower, quarterly budget allocations, re-accommodating visitors, and getting rid of those journalists together with Raimondo.

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: But our main goal remains the same — to rebuild the Fontaine Research Institute and work hard for the well-being of all the people of the Court of Fontaine.

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: You go and do what you need to do. The Institute will always welcome you!
